class_id: an OCR page detector's memory-exhaustion allocation failure is re-raised as a generic runtime error, so a resource-ceiling OOM is misclassified as a content failure
feature: scraper's OCR pipeline: memory_guard.is_memory_exhaustion + ocr_pages.read_page_with_fallback, called by the extractor, anchor reports (ocr_pdf_page_boxes) and corrigendum pages (ocr_pdf_pages)
symptom: RapidOCR's text detector allocates memory proportional to the full page-image size (limit_type: min); under the extractor's RLIMIT_AS ceiling, a large scanned page cannot allocate inside onnxruntime. onnxruntime re-raises that allocation failure as a generic `ONNXRuntimeError 'inference failed'`, with the real `bad allocation` text surviving only on `__cause__`/`__context__`. A classifier that reads only the outer message therefore reports a content/parse failure (exit 1) instead of a resource-ceiling failure (exit 3), and the retry loop treats it as content -- so it retries the same oversized page at the same size every time and fails identically forever, blocking the whole document.
first_seen: 2026-09-25/26 -- #1046, PR #1195. Four staging HARD_FAILURE documents shared this exact stack: kanohar-electricals-ltd PROSPECTUS (6 retries), elevate-campuses-ltd RHP (8), swastika-infra-ltd DRHP (8), runwal-enterprises-ltd PRICE_BAND_AD (4).
fix_prs: #1195: memory_guard.is_memory_exhaustion walks the __cause__/__context__ chain so a wrapped allocation failure is correctly classified; ocr_pages.read_page_with_fallback re-renders a failing page at progressively smaller long-edge sizes (2400px, then 1600px) before giving up, covering all three ocr_pages callers.
detection_check: none yet named beyond the classifier fix itself; a nightly count of documents blocked with an OCR-classified memory-exhaustion cause, expected to fall to 0 after the fix deploys, would close the loop.
